scenario: A music industry report covers only artists who have sustained more than 5,000 monthly listeners on streaming platforms, as lower figures are deemed commercially insignificant. A talent scout uses the report's average to set discovery thresholds.

data.description: Report covers only artists with > 5,000 monthly listeners. Listener counts assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = 4,000.

question: Covered artists average 11,000 monthly listeners. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean monthly listener count Î¼ across ALL artists releasing music (including those below the threshold), and (b) the fraction of all artists covered in the report.
naive_answer: The typical artist has about 11,000 monthly listeners since that is the report average.
naive_trap: About 9% of active artists are below 5,000 listeners and excluded. The true mean is 10,257 â€” 743 lower. A scout using 11,000 as a baseline benchmark is already filtering out the bottom tail before setting thresholds.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: E[X|X>5]=Î¼+4Â·Î»((5-Î¼)/4)=11. Step 2: Solve numerically for Î¼â‰ˆ10.257k. Step 3: Fraction covered=Î¦Ì„((5-10.257)/4)=Î¦Ì„(-1.314)â‰ˆ0.906.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(5-mu)/4; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+4*norm.pdf(a)/sf-11 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,10,10.9)
assert abs(mu-10.257)<0.15
assert abs(norm.sf((5-mu)/4)-0.9056)<0.01
